description: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets over time, categorized by the number of languages they contain. The horizontal axis, labeled "Year," displays chronological categories from 2012 to 2021, followed by a final unlabeled category marked by a solid gray rectangle on the axis. The vertical axis, labeled "Number of datasets," employs a logarithmic scale (base 10) with tick labels and major grid lines at $10^1$ and $10^2$. The chart features grouped vertical bars, with the grouping arrangement and colors defined by a legend titled "Languages": blue bars represent datasets with "1" language, and orange bars represent datasets with "2+" languages. For the years 2012 through 2016, only blue bars are present, starting at approximately 2 datasets in 2012 and increasing to roughly 12 datasets in 2016. From 2017 to 2021, both categories are represented in each group. The blue bars (1 language) show a consistent upward trend, culminating in the tallest bar on the chart at approximately 150 datasets in 2021. The orange bars (2+ languages) fluctuate, with the lowest value of approximately 2 datasets in 2018 and the highest value of approximately 20 datasets in 2020. The final, unlabeled category on the far right is visually distinguished from the rest of the data through faded colors, containing a light blue bar indicating roughly 30 datasets and a light orange bar indicating approximately 2 datasets.
